strengths: Multi-component integration and bring-up debugging on real hardware - COFFIN capstone three-layer pipeline (Flutter client / Flask-SocketIO edge server / Jetson+Arduino controller over one WebSocket fabric) plus 'resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); 100% pick reliability (10/10)'. This is literally integration and commissioning work.

C++ on real-time hardware - two-link IK on Arduino in C++; STM32 bare-metal C (GPIO/TIM2/ADC1/I2C1, 3.68KB Flash, deterministic 1Hz); Object Tracking Turret with FreeRTOS mutexes and interrupt-driven UART.

Operator-facing UI over live hardware telemetry - Flask-SocketIO + WebSocket fabric, Flutter mobile client, PyQt/Matplotlib real-time DAQ GUI at BARC. Right shape as the Angular half, wrong framework.
Physical sensor integration and calibration - dual VL53L0X ToF via TCA9548A I2C mux with range-gated contact detection; ADXL345 3-DoF motion to HID with jitter resolved by software calibration.
Controls and kinematics - hand-derived DH tables for UR5e/AL5B, validated against MoveIt/RViz, collision-free trajectories on physical UR5e, <2mm repeatability over 10 trials.
Simulation-before-hardware habit (closest thing to SIL) - CARLA Town02 validation with 30 vehicles and zero collisions, Proteus verification of STM32 firmware, full ABB RobotStudio workcell in RAPID.
real_gaps: Angular is a true zero, not a near-miss: no TypeScript, no JavaScript, no SPA, no component/DI framework, no npm build tooling anywhere in the profile. Flutter is Dart, Flask is server-side Python, PyQt is desktop. Angular is named in the single primary responsibility line, so this is roughly 35-45% of the actual day job, not 1 of 12 checkboxes.

Automated software testing is a listed responsibility with zero backing: no GoogleTest, CTest, pytest, CI pipeline, regression suite, or test harness anywhere. Benchmarking measures performance; tests assert correctness and gate merges. Different discipline.

SIL specifically - CARLA/Proteus/RobotStudio were hand-driven demo and validation environments, not an automated rig that compiles production control software against a plant model and reports pass/fail into a build. The gap is the automation and plant-model discipline, not the concept.

Production object-oriented C++ at scale - his C++ is embedded procedural (bare-metal register writes, Arduino sketches) plus CUDA kernels. The JD's 'component-based, object-oriented development', 'interprets functional and technical blueprints', and 'participates in code reviews' imply a large existing C++ codebase. Nothing in the profile shows working inside someone else's large codebase; everything is greenfield and solo or small-team.

GNSS and machine-guidance domain is absent - GPS, optical total stations, lasers, sonics, grade control. Kinematics is not geodesy; expect an unanswerable question on coordinate frames, sensor fusion, or accuracy budgets.

Zero full-time experience - seven entries, all internships or fellowships, longest about 10 months. Survivable at this competency bar, but 'commissioning' carries a customer-facing, own-it-in-the-field flavor that research-scope work does not demonstrate.
